To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Latinx students in student organizations develop social and cultural capital that assists them in navigating college, academics and career development.

Latinx based organizations cultivate social and emotional support among participants, and that this support is critical for students to develop a sense of belonging in college, navigate academics, and career preparation.
Latinx based organizations provide a space for Latinx students to acquire and share cultural, social, and symbolic forms of capital.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which Latinx students acquire capital in Latinx student organizations.
the ways in which social and cultural capital is shared among peers and how this process assists Latinx students in navigating college, academic and professional development.
understanding how students in Latinx organizations acquire and share social, cultural, and economic capital in the pursuit of academic success.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Latinx student organizations are a vital resource for first generation students in the process of social and academic integration in college.
Latinx based student organizations are an important source of capital that assists first generation college students in navigating their academic and career development.
Latinx student organizations are a source of social capital that helps students develop cultural capital to navigate college.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Latinx student organizations provide a space for participants to share social, cultural and human capital with peers.
Latinx student organizations serve as a space for the acquisition of social and cultural capital that is relevant for college and career success.
Latinx based organizations are important for students' success because they help students develop social and cultural capital.
The main takeaway from our work is that
these organizations serve as a bridge between the emotional and academic needs of participants by creating a sense of belonging and community.
Latinx student organizations are a valuable asset to students and their families, and they should be supported by the university and the community.
Latinx students in our study found that Latinx based organizations provided a space for them to acquire capital that was not readily available to them outside of the organization.
